# Review Autopilot

> A human-run review service for local businesses: an audit of the business’s own public reviews with recovery and reply drafts the owner approves before anything is sent, an every-customer review request flow, and an optional monthly loop. $149 setup audit, one time; the loop, if taken, is $29/mo per location, month-to-month.

Review Autopilot is a product by Northbeam Builds, a small studio in Austin, TX that builds websites and AI tools for local service businesses. Company site: https://northbeambuilds.com

## What it is

Reviews run on a loop whether the owner works it or not: a job goes well or badly, a customer says something or stays silent, and the next customer reads whatever accumulated. Review Autopilot works the whole loop. The setup ($149, one time) is an audit of the business’s own public review profile: every unhappy reviewer (1–3 stars) sorted HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW for recovery by printed rules, private recovery drafts and public reply drafts written for each, not-a-candidate cases labelled with their handling, an every-customer request flow set up, and a testimonial widget installed on the business’s website. The optional loop ($29/mo per location, month-to-month, agreed separately) keeps it running monthly: new reviews checked and sorted, drafts written for the owner’s approval, the month’s review requests prepared from completed jobs, widget additions, and a one-page report.

Two rules are not negotiable: nothing is ever offered in exchange for removing or changing a review, and reviews are never bought, incentivised, gated, or suppressed — every customer is offered the public review link on the same terms.

Honest method notes: the sorting engine is rules-based software (v1), not AI, and it is a prioritisation tool, not a prediction; no outcome — a reviewer responding, returning, or updating a review — is promised anywhere. Drafts arrive as a document; the owner reads, edits, and sends; nothing goes out in the owner’s name without their say-so. The loop is a human-run monthly service, not a dashboard, and it does not send live alerts.

## Who it is for

For: Owners whose reviews sit unanswered because the work comes first.; Happy customers never get asked, so the profile is mostly the unhappy ones.; Owners who want the replies written but the final say kept.
Not for: Anyone who wants bad reviews removed or buried — not offered at any price.; Anyone who wants a dashboard and live alerts — this is a document and a monthly service.

## Price

$149 flat, one time, for the setup audit. No monthly fee for the setup. Optional follow-on, afterwards only: the loop at $29/mo per business location, month-to-month; additional locations quoted per business before any agreement; no agency tier, no contract. Live by the date we agree, or your setup fee comes back in full — guaranteed. If the audit is not delivered by the date agreed, the $149 is refunded in full; if the buyer’s go-ahead/profile access isn’t completed within 14 days of purchase, the order is refunded in full.
Start: email northbeambuilds@gmail.com with your public review-profile link, or use the company contact page: https://northbeambuilds.com/contact/
Free sample: email your profile link and ask for the sample — the first page of the audit (unhappy reviews sorted, one recovery draft written), free, no card.

## How it works

1. The owner gives the go-ahead and a link to their public review profile.
2. We pull the reviews, sort every unhappy reviewer by the printed rules, and draft the private recovery messages and public replies.
3. A person hand-checks every draft against the review it answers; the request flow is set up and the testimonial widget installed.
4. The owner receives the audit document, reads and edits the drafts, and sends and posts them. Nothing goes out in their name without them.

## What is included

- The recovery list: every 1–3 star reviewer classified HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW with the reason in plain English, plus not-a-candidate cases with their handling.
- Private recovery message drafts and public reply drafts.
- Thank-you notes for five-star reviewers.
- The request flow: one identical note to every customer after a completed job — same wording, same public link.
- The testimonial widget installed on the business’s website, showing approved testimonials with the average computed from what’s displayed.
- On the loop ($29/mo per location): monthly profile check with new reviews sorted the same way; recovery + reply drafts for approval; the month’s review requests prepared; widget additions; a one-page monthly report.
- Delivered by the date agreed — the clock starts when payment, go-ahead, and profile link are all in, whichever comes last.

## Questions and answers

- Q: Will this get my bad reviews removed?
  A: No — and that is not what this is. Anyone who promises removal is selling something you should not buy. Review Autopilot helps you answer well, make a genuine recovery attempt with the customers who can be reached, and earn more reviews honestly. Removal is never offered, asked for, or traded for, and nothing is ever offered in exchange for removing or changing a review.
- Q: Who writes the replies — a person or a program?
  A: Both, in that order of importance. A rules-based program sorts your reviews — how recent, whether you’ve responded, whether the complaint is specific, whether the reviewer says it was resolved — and the rules are printed in your audit so you can check every sorting decision. A person then hand-checks every draft against the review it answers before you see it. It is not AI, and the sorting is a way to decide where your effort goes first, not a prediction about any reviewer.
- Q: Do you post the replies or send the messages for me?
  A: No. Everything arrives as drafts in a document. You read them, edit them into your own voice, and you send and post them yourself. Nothing ever goes out in your name without your say-so — there is no approval app or button, because the approval is you, reading it.
- Q: Is asking customers for reviews allowed?
  A: Asking is what every platform expects. Paying for reviews, offering something in exchange, or selectively asking only happy customers — “review gating” — is what platforms prohibit. Review Autopilot asks every customer the same way: one note after a completed job, the same wording and the same public review link for everyone, whatever they honestly thought of the job. Unhappy customers also get a private route to you, because fixing their problem is the point — and they get the same public link as everyone else.
- Q: How do you reach unhappy reviewers privately?
  A: Through contact details from your own job records, if you have them — the drafts are written for that channel. We don’t obtain, buy, or look up customer contact details.
- Q: What if some of my reviews are fake, or from a competitor?
  A: They’re classified as not-a-candidate, with the indicators noted, and the audit tells you to flag them through the platform’s own reporting route instead of engaging them publicly. We can’t get them removed and won’t pretend otherwise.
- Q: Where do the reviews come from?
  A: Your own public review profile, pulled with your go-ahead after you order. No third-party data, no private customer information.
- Q: What does the audit need from me?
  A: Your go-ahead, a link to your public review profile, your business name as it appears there, and the owner name to use in draft sign-offs. For the widget, access to place one snippet on your website — or your web person’s email.
- Q: What does it cost?
  A: $149 once for the setup audit. No monthly fee for the setup. Afterwards, only if you want it, the loop is $29/mo per business location, month-to-month — additional locations are quoted per business before any agreement. There is no contract and no agency tier.
- Q: Is there a contract?
  A: No. The audit is a one-time $149, delivered by the date we agree — the clock starts when your payment, your go-ahead, and your review-profile link are all in — whichever comes last — or the $149 comes back in full. If the loop is ever taken, it is month-to-month and separate; cancel any time and the audit, the drafts, and the installed widget remain yours.
